page.layout: One printed page (right-hand page of an opening), with a running head at top, two woodcut illustrations of stones occupying the upper and middle area, the main text block below them, and a catchword/signature line at the foot. Faint show-through text from the reverse side appears in the left margin and centre; it is not transcribed. No marginal notes are legible.

main_text.p: convexa eius parte vestigia divisionum, aequales in testa Testudinis cernuntur: verum exterior tunica huius lapidis, ut ita vocem, substantia multum distat ab interiori corpore, nam cum illud durissimum & silicium sit, illa paulo est mollior. Hoc quoque in illis lapidibus observavi, (habeo enim plures & unum triplo maiorem priore, quem & exprimen-

page.notes: The woodcut illustrations show two stones; the upper one is a rounded stone with vein-like markings, the lower one a stone with a cross-sectioned, cellular surface. The first line of text is partly obscured by the lower illustration; "convexa" and "aequales" are read with some doubt, and "quales" may be the printed form. The line "unum triplo maiorem priore, quem & exprimen-" is followed by the catchword "dum". Show-through from the reverse page is faint in the left and centre and was disregarded.
